title: Rosalind Franklin Knew Her Famous DNA Photo Was Special, Study Says
summary:
DNA carries the instructions for every living thing. In 1962, three scientists won a Nobel Prize for showing that DNA is shaped like a double helix, a twisted ladder. Their work used X-ray photos taken by another scientist, Rosalind Franklin.

A new study looked at Franklin's notes and photos. Historian Alistair Sponsel and scientist Brian Sutton say she understood more than people thought.

Her most famous picture is called Photograph 51. Some stories said she did not think it was important. But her notes for an earlier photo, Photograph 49, mention a possible helix shape. The same day she saw it, she started a sharper photo of the same sample.

Sponsel said her extra effort was "a sign she knew she had something really important on her hands."

Franklin died in 1958, which made her unable to share the later prize. The study suggests she found DNA's helix shape, but not the full double helix.
why_it_matters: It reminds us that everyone who helps with a discovery deserves credit.
